title: Astronomers Found a Planet Younger Than Our Species. It Shouldn't Exist Yet

scenes.text: This giant planet is younger than the human species.
It's called Elias 2-24 b, and it's less than one million years old.
Every planet found before it was at least five million years old.
It's a Jupiter-sized world, about 450 light-years away, carving a gap in a ring of dust.
The problem: models say a giant that far from its star needs about five million years to form.
This one did it in under one. Our best theory of how planets are born is missing something.

description:
Elias 2-24 b, about 450 light-years away, is less than a million years old, the youngest planet ever confirmed.
Giant planets that far from their star were thought to need about 5 million years to form. Found with ALMA, ESO's Very Large Telescope and Keck archive images, published September 2026.
How do you think it formed so fast?
first_comment: Homo sapiens is about 300,000 years old, so this planet only beat us by a few hundred thousand years. What space record should we cover next?
